basis: Intestinal egg granulomas define S. mansoni infection; substantial hepatosplenic fibrosis occurs in only ~5-10%, not most infections.

decisions.hepatic: none: egg deposition alone need not impair liver function; substantial hepatosplenic fibrosis occurs in ~5-10%.

basis: Glial tumor of posterior pituitary/stalk; optic apparatus compression causes visual field loss in 30-79% (HPO).

decisions.ocular: involved: compressive optic apparatus dysfunction produces visual field defects in 30-79% (HPO), rather than a transient visual symptom.

basis: Vertebral malformations and learning disability characterize the symptomatic phenotype; most prenatal mosaics are normal, making penetrance uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: primary: learning disability characterizes the described symptomatic phenotype; penetrance across predominantly normal prenatal mosaics is uncertain.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: vertebral malformations characterize the described symptomatic phenotype; uncertain penetrance precludes claiming common secondary organ damage.

basis: Spinal cord/meningeal herniation through a vertebral defect; neurogenic bladder (~70-90%) is separately diagnosed neural urinary dysfunction, not direct urinary tissue injury.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder (~70-90%) reflects spinal denervation and is separately diagnosed; direct renal or urinary tissue damage is not established in >=30%.

basis: Idiopathic inflammatory outer-retinal disease; inflammation and a suspected immune trigger do not establish infectious or autoimmune causation.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: immune-mediated pathogenesis is proposed, but inflammatory classification alone does not establish infection or an autoimmune/immune-mediated disease.

basis: Inherited bile-transport disorder causing intrahepatic cholestasis; classified under inborn bilirubin metabolism disorders. Microvillus inclusion disease is a distinct phenotype.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: inherited intrahepatic bile-transport dysfunction is an inborn metabolic disorder, supported by the bilirubin-metabolism ancestor.

basis: Pituicyte-derived glial tumor of posterior pituitary; optic apparatus compression causes visual impairment in approximately 60-70% of reported cases.

decisions.ocular: involved: direct optic apparatus compression causes visual impairment in approximately 60-70% of reported cases.

basis: Neurodegenerative ataxia subtype defined by peripheral amyotrophy (80-99% HPO); ophthalmoplegia is neurologic, and bladder/vestibular dysfunction occurs in <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: peripheral amyotrophy defines this subtype and represents established muscle wasting (80-99% HPO), despite its neurogenic origin.

basis: Fiedler myocarditis classically denotes idiopathic giant-cell myocarditis, an immune-mediated destructive myocardial disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the Fiedler eponym classically denotes immune-mediated giant-cell myocarditis; its idiopathic designation does not exclude that mechanism.

basis: Forebrain/callosal malformation; maxillary hypoplasia 20/20 and dental malocclusion 11/14 support skeletal/dental involvement. Panhypopituitarism 3/11 (~27%) is below threshold.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental malocclusion affects 11/14 (~79%); teeth and occlusion fall within the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: panhypopituitarism is reported in 3/11 (~27%); pituitary involvement is not required by this concept's definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: maxillary hypoplasia in 20/20 is a common structural bone malformation; isolated facial appearance alone would not suffice.
